**The Last Letter**

I found it tucked between the pages of an old, yellowed novel in the attic. The book smelled of dust and something faintly metallic—like old blood. My grandmother had told me never to touch the things up there, but curiosity had always been my downfall.

The letter was written in a hand I didn’t recognize. The ink had bled through the paper, as if the writer had pressed too hard. The words were scrawled in jagged strokes:

*"They’re coming. The ones who don’t sleep. The ones who whisper in the dark. I saw them last night. They were watching me. I tried to run, but they were faster. They have no faces, only hollow eyes. They know my name. They know where I live. They’re coming for me. Please, if you find this, burn it. Burn everything. Don’t let them find you."*

I held it to the light, and the ink smudged. The words blurred, as if the paper itself was trying to erase the truth. My grandmother’s voice echoed in my head: *"Some things are better left forgotten."*

But I couldn’t forget. Not now.

I called the police. They laughed. Said it was just an old letter. A prank. A ghost story.

But the whispers started the next night.

They came from the walls. From the floorboards. From the shadows where no shadow should be.

And they were calling my name.

I ran. I hid. But they were always one step behind.

Then, one morning, I found the letter again. This time, it was in my own handwriting.

I had written it.

I had written it.

I had written it.

And the cycle began anew.
